t: You're looking at the London Troops War Memorial, standing in front of the Royal Exchange in the City of London. It commemorates the men of London who fought in the First and Second World Wars. Three people made it. Sir Aston Webb, the architect, also designed the main face of Buckingham Palace and the Victoria and Albert Museum. Alfred Drury, a sculptor of the New Sculpture movement, made many war memorials and figures across central London. William Silver Frith was a sculptor too.
